description:
src/memory.rs:290-320 — MemoryBackend exposes four public methods whose
intent is test-fixture mutation:

    pub fn set_default_calendar_for_test(&self, account_id: &str, default_id: Option<&str>);
    pub fn set_default_participant_identity_for_test(&self, account_id: &str, default_id: Option<&str>);
    pub fn get_default_calendar(&self, account_id: &str) -> Option<Id>;
    pub fn get_default_participant_identity(&self, account_id: &str) -> Option<Id>;

The `_for_test` suffix on the first two declares intent. But the visibility
modifier is `pub`, and the only gate is `#[cfg(feature = "memory")]` (the
module declaration in lib.rs:44-45). Any downstream consumer who enables
`memory` for a smoke test or example sees these in their IDE's
autocomplete, has them surfaced by `cargo doc`, and can call them in
production code.

The canonical mail-server (crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs) does NOT
expose any `*_for_test` or `get_*_for_test` methods. Mail's test seams that
need to read/mutate backend state live in `tests/common/mod.rs` (e.g.
`FaultyBackend`), where they are invisible to downstream crates.

What goes wrong for the caller:

  1. A consumer enabling the `memory` feature for a non-test use (demo,
     example, smoke test, integration scaffold) gets a backend with
     "test-only" mutation knobs in its public API.
  2. Once published with these signatures, removing `set_default_calendar_for_test`
     or renaming `get_default_calendar` is a SemVer break. The maintainer
     is locked in.
  3. The `_for_test` naming convention is informal — it does not prevent
     downstream consumers from using them. A consumer writing a "test"
     today that ships to production tomorrow imports the methods and
     depends on their behaviour.
  4. The signature divergence from canonical mail-server (which has no such
     methods) means a contributor cookie-cutting a calendars-style memory
     fixture into mail-server has nowhere to put it; conversely, propagating
     mail's "no fixture knobs" policy to calendars requires deleting four
     pub methods.

Fix options:

  (a) Gate behind a stricter `#[cfg(test)]`-only or `pub(crate)` boundary;
      move test consumers into `tests/common/`. This is the canonical
      mail-server pattern.
  (b) Add a separate `test-fixtures` cargo feature, gate these methods
      behind it, document that the feature is unstable and intended only
      for downstream test code.
  (c) Keep them `pub` under `memory`, but rename to `set_default_calendar` /
      `set_default_participant_identity` (drop `_for_test`) and document
      that MemoryBackend is itself a demonstration backend whose mutation
      knobs are part of its supported API surface. Consistent with the
      "MemoryBackend is reference impl, not production" framing.

(a) matches canonical-template policy. (c) is the most honest framing of
current behaviour. (b) is a compromise that preserves the test-only intent.

P2 — published-API design decision, not a present-day bug.
title: MemoryBackend exposes set_default_*_for_test and get_default_* as pub API (gated only by feature='memory')
